issues.problem: Printful publishes a general limit of 120 API calls per minute, with lower limits for some resource-intensive endpoints.
issues.suggestion: Set to "120 requests per minute generally; lower endpoint-specific limits may apply."

issues.problem: The current store-information endpoints are /stores and /stores/{id}; /store is not the documented endpoint. The shown response also does not match the current /stores response shape.
issues.suggestion: Use "curl -sS -H \"Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY\" https://api.printful.com/stores" and show result as an array with paging, or call /stores/{id} for one store.

issues.problem: The value "..." is incorrect. PubChem explicitly asks clients not to exceed 5 requests per second and may throttle excessive traffic.
issues.suggestion: Set to "Maximum 5 requests per second; automated throttling and 503 responses may apply."

issues.problem: PUG-REST returns MolecularWeight as a JSON string, not a number.
issues.suggestion: Change MolecularWeight to "180.16".

issues.problem: Current Channels Sandbox limits are published, not unknown.
issues.suggestion: Set to "200,000 messages per day and 100 concurrent connections."

issues.problem: Pusher has published paid Channels plans, so null is inaccurate.
issues.suggestion: Record the current self-serve plans, starting with Startup at $49/month, Pro at $99/month, and Business at $299/month, plus higher tiers.

issues.problem: A successful event trigger without the info parameter returns an empty JSON object; HTTP status 200 is not returned as a status field in the body.
PyPI does publish its current policy: the JSON, RSS, and Index APIs presently have no edge rate limit, although irresponsible consumers may be blocked and XML-RPC may be limited.
issues.suggestion: Set to "Currently no edge rate limiting for JSON, RSS, or Index APIs; respect caching/ETag guidance and identify requests with User-Agent."

issues.problem: The request retrieves the latest requests metadata, but the shown version 2.32.3 is stale; the current response reports 2.34.2.
issues.suggestion: Update the version to 2.34.2 or omit volatile version-specific values from the snippet.

issues.problem: The official hosted API has been repeatedly unreachable, with unresolved outage and DNS reports through 2026; a July 2026 check also found no HTTP response.
issues.suggestion: Mark as unavailable, discontinued, or unreliable rather than operational, unless a fresh live probe proves recovery.

issues.problem: Although this was the canonical host, api.quotable.io is not currently a functioning public API root.
issues.suggestion: Do not list a hosted base URL unless service is restored; present the GitHub project as self-hostable instead.

issues.problem: The project documentation publishes a limit of 180 requests per minute per IP.
issues.suggestion: Set to "180 requests per minute per IP when the hosted service is available."

issues.problem: The claim that no quota is published conflicts with the documented 180-requests-per-minute limit.
issues.suggestion: Set to "Free/open-source; hosted service documents 180 requests per minute per IP, but is currently unavailable."

issues.problem: Radar expects the API key itself in the Authorization header. Its current examples do not use the Bearer scheme.
issues.suggestion: Use "Publishable or secret API key sent directly as Authorization: prj_test_pk_..., prj_live_pk_..., prj_test_sk_..., or prj_live_sk_...; secret keys are server-side only."

issues.problem: Radar documentation publishes a free allowance of up to 100,000 API requests per month rather than an unknown limit.
issues.suggestion: Set to "Up to 100,000 API requests per month; other product-specific limits may also apply."

issues.problem: Radar offers paid Enterprise access, so null incorrectly implies no paid option.
issues.suggestion: Set to "Paid Enterprise/custom pricing available."

issues.problem: Radar publishes endpoint-specific default rate limits; they are not wholly unpublished.
issues.suggestion: State that limits vary by endpoint, commonly from 1 to 150 requests per second, and record the relevant endpoint-specific value where possible.

issues.problem: The 20,000-request allowance is correct but omits material current conditions: the public pricing page limits the Free plan to personal/non-commercial projects and requires backlinks to RAWG where its data is used.
issues.suggestion: Set to "Up to 20,000 requests/month for personal and hobby/non-commercial projects; attribution and active backlinks are required."

issues.problem: RAWG publishes paid plans, so null is inaccurate.
issues.suggestion: Set to "Business: $149/month for up to 50,000 requests/month and commercial use; Enterprise: custom pricing, up to 1,000,000 requests/month."

issues.problem: Free test mode is a sandbox, not a free production tier. Successful live payments incur transaction/platform fees.
issues.suggestion: Set free_tier to false, or explicitly model this as "free sandbox/test mode only; live usage is transaction-priced."

issues.problem: RCSB explicitly states that all APIs are rate-limited and recommends starting with only a handful of requests per second, even though it does not publish one universal numeric ceiling.
issues.suggestion: Set to "Rate limited; begin with a handful of requests per second, handle HTTP 429, and use retry with exponential backoff; exact thresholds vary or are unpublished."
